NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 7 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 25 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 22, 10:22 AM ET

George Kittle is the top-projected tight end on the Week 7 DraftKings main slate at 17.4 DraftKings points for $5,700, at Atlanta. Trey McBride (17.3, $7,400) and Brock Bowers (16.6, $7,700) are next.

Cade Otton returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 3.13 projected points per $1,000 at $3,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 22, 10:22 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 7

George Kittle, SF at ATL ($5,700)

George Kittle carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 17.4 DraftKings points at $5,700. That is 0.1 points clear of Trey McBride. The model gives him 7.8 targets on 22.3 routes. The salary works out to 3.06 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Kittle averaged 17.4 points with a simulated floor of 6.3 and a ceiling of 35.6, and he holds 29% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 4.5-point favorite on the road against Atlanta, with an implied team total of 27.5 in a game totaled at 50.5.

Trey McBride, ARI vs DEN ($7,400)

Trey McBride projects 2nd at the position with 17.3 DraftKings points at $7,400. The model gives him 10.3 targets on 37.5 routes. The salary works out to 2.34 projected points per $1,000, 9th of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 6.6 and a ceiling of 36.1, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 4.5-point underdog at home against Denver, with an implied team total of 19.5 in a game totaled at 43.5.

Value: Cade Otton, TB at CAR ($3,100)

Cade Otton projects for 9.7 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 3.13 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 14 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 6.5 targets on 30.7 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Otton averaged 9.6 points with a simulated floor of 1.5 and a ceiling of 25.2, and he holds 16% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Tampa Bay is a 3.5-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 20.5 in a game totaled at 44.5.
